title: 别云间
author: 夏完淳
intro: Written by a sixteen-year-old resistance fighter on his way to execution, saying goodbye to his hometown. It is short, plain and unbearably calm — a boy who knows he will die and promises to come back as a spirit to keep fighting.
analysis: 明朝灭亡后，清兵南下，少年夏完淳跟着父亲和老师起兵抗清，前后三年。后来他被捕，押往南京受审，临走前写下这首诗告别家乡云间（今上海松江）。开头说自己在外奔走三年，今天成了囚犯——“南冠”本是楚国人戴的帽子，后来成了囚犯的代称。第二联最有力量：山河破碎，泪流不尽，谁还能说天地宽广？天地再大，已经没有他的容身之处。第三联平静地说出死亡——“泉路”就是黄泉路，他知道自己快死了，真正难的是离开家乡。最后一联不写悲伤，而写希望：等我坚毅的魂魄回来，要在空中看见招魂的灵旗、抗清的战旗。全诗没有一句喊口号，却让人读出一个十六岁少年的勇气。
analysisEn: After the Ming dynasty fell in 1644, the Manchu Qing armies swept south. The teenage Xia Wanchun joined his father and his teacher in armed resistance for three years. Captured in 1647, he was sent to Nanjing for trial, and before leaving he wrote this farewell to his hometown, Yunjian (today’s Songjiang, in Shanghai). The opening is factual: three years on the road, and now he wears the “southern cap” — an old phrase for a prisoner, from a captive of the state of Chu who kept wearing his native hat. The second couplet is the heart of the poem: rivers and mountains soaked in endless tears — who says heaven and earth are wide? For him the world has shrunk to nothing. The third couplet speaks of death with almost no emotion: he knows the road to the underworld is near; what is hard is leaving home. The last couplet turns grief into resolve: on the day his unyielding spirit returns, it will look for the battle flags in the sky. There are no slogans here, just a sixteen-year-old facing death with his head up — which is why Chinese readers still find it so moving.
background: Xia Wanchun (1631–1647) was a child prodigy from Songjiang who fought against the Qing conquest. He was captured in 1647 and executed in Nanjing at the age of sixteen; this poem was written as he was taken away from home.
pronunciation: 冠：南冠 nán guān（名词，帽子，不读 guàn）。羁 jī。看：本诗押平声韵（冠、宽、难、看），按格律读 kān；现代口语多读 kàn。网站暂注 kān。机器朗读把“冠”“看”替换为同音字，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行文本（《夏完淳集》）。题目一作《别云间》，云间是松江的古称。

lines.en: Three years I roamed, a man without a home;

lines.lit: today again in the southern cap.
lines.en: today I wear a prisoner’s cap.

lines.lit: Endless tears for mountains and rivers —
lines.en: Endless tears for our broken land —

lines.lit: who says heaven and earth are wide!
lines.en: who still says the world is wide?

lines.lit: I already know the road to the springs below is near;
lines.en: I know the road to the dead is close;

lines.lit: wanting to leave my homeland, it is hard.
lines.en: what is hard is leaving home.

lines.lit: On the day my resolute spirit returns,
lines.en: When my stubborn soul comes back one day,

lines.lit: I will look for the spirit banners in the sky.
lines.en: I’ll watch for our banners in the sky.

words.en: to live away from home; to wander
words.note: 羁：停留、受牵制。现代汉语书面语“羁旅”仍用。
典故：春秋时楚国人钟仪被俘仍戴楚国帽子，后来“南冠”成了囚犯的代称。
现代汉语仍说“大好山河”。
现代汉语书面语“欲望”“欲言又止”。
古代招魂用的旗，也指出征的战旗。

words.en: the sky; up in the air

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: “山河”指整个国家；山河还在，国家已亡，所以满是泪水。
imagery.en: “Mountains and rivers” stand for the whole country — the land is still there, but the nation is lost.

imagery.name: 泪
imagery.zh: “山河泪”是为国家流的泪，不是为自己。
imagery.en: These are tears for the country, not for himself.

imagery.name: 天地
imagery.zh: 天地本来宽广，可对一个即将赴死的亡国少年来说，已无处容身。
imagery.en: Heaven and earth should be vast, yet for a boy about to die for a lost country there is no room left anywhere.
